verses.text: I am the man that has seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.
He has led me and caused me to walk in darkness, and not in light.
Surely against me he turns his hand again and again all day long.
He has made my flesh and my skin old; he has broken my bones.
He has built against me, and surrounded me with gall and travail.
He has made me to dwell in dark places, as those that have been long dead.
He has walled me about, that I can’t go out; he has made my chain heavy.
Yes, when I cry, and call for help, he shuts out my prayer.
He has walled up my ways with cut stone; he has made my paths crooked.
He is to me as a bear lying in wait, as a lion in secret places.
He has turned aside my ways, and pulled me in pieces; he has made me desolate.
He has bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.
He has caused the shafts of his quiver to enter into my kidneys.
I have become a derision to all my people, and their song all day long.
He has filled me with bitterness. He has sated me with wormwood.
He has also broken my teeth with gravel stones; he has covered me with ashes.
You have removed my soul far off from peace; I forgot prosperity.
I said, “My strength has perished, along with my expectation from Yahweh.”
Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.
My soul still remembers them, and is bowed down within me.
This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.
It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail.
They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
“Yahweh is my portion,” says my soul. “Therefore I will hope in him.”
Yahweh is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Yahweh.
It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.
Let him sit alone and keep silence, because he has laid it on him.
Let him put his mouth in the dust, if so be there may be hope.
Let him give his cheek to him who strikes him; let him be filled full with reproach.
For the Lord will not cast off forever.
For though he cause grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
For he does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.
To crush under foot all the prisoners of the earth,
To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the Most High,
To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord doesn’t approve.
Who is he who says, and it comes to pass, when the Lord doesn’t command it?
Doesn’t evil and good come out of the mouth of the Most High?
Why does a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?
Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to Yahweh.
Let us lift up our heart with our hands to God  in the heavens.
“We have transgressed and have rebelled. You have not pardoned.
“You have covered us with anger and pursued us. You have killed. You have not pitied.
You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through.
You have made us an off-scouring and refuse in the middle of the peoples.
“All our enemies have opened their mouth wide against us.
Terror and the pit have come on us, devastation and destruction.”
My eye runs down with streams of water, for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
My eye pours down, and doesn’t cease, without any intermission,
until Yahweh looks down, and sees from heaven.
My eye affects my soul, because of all the daughters of my city.
They have chased me relentlessly like a bird, those who are my enemies without cause.
They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and have cast a stone on me.
Waters flowed over my head; I said, I am cut off.
I called on your name, Yahweh, out of the lowest dungeon.
You heard my voice: “Don’t hide your ear from my sighing, and my cry.”
You came near in the day that I called on you; you said, “Don’t be afraid.”
Lord, you have pleaded the causes of my soul; you have redeemed my life.
Yahweh, you have seen my wrong. Judge my cause.
You have seen all their vengeance and all their devices against me.
You have heard their reproach, Yahweh, and all their devices against me,
The lips of those that rose up against me, and their device against me all day long.
You see their sitting down and their rising up; I am their song.
You will render to them a recompense, Yahweh, according to the work of their hands.
You will give them hardness of heart, your curse to them.
You will pursue them in anger, and destroy them from under the heavens of Yahweh.

footnotes.content: The speaker begins in his own skin—not as a distant theologian but as one who has drunk the cup of God's discipline. There's weight in 'the man that has seen' because affliction teaches you things abstract knowledge never can. He knows the rod not as doctrine but as lived weight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Darkness without light—not as poetic exaggeration but the actual felt condition of one cut off from God's face. The Lord Himself has led him into this place, not abandoned him to wander. That's the precise sting: the darkness comes from His hand, not chaos.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again and again—not one blow but the turning of His hand repeatedly, all day long. This is the loneliness of persistent correction. Yet notice: it is *His* hand doing it, not Satan's or fate's. The Lord is present even in repeated correction.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The speaker's body itself has become old under affliction—flesh wasted, bones broken. This is not metaphor; it's the real price of captivity and siege. Yet he calls it by name before God. The physical wreckage is part of what must be spoken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Built against him like siege works, surrounded by bitterness—gall and travail are his diet. He is hemmed in, not by accident but by divine intention. The Lord has constructed this place of affliction, and the speaker is its prisoner.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dark places, the dwelling of the long dead—he compares his condition to the grave itself. This is not exaggeration when a city is starving and its people dying. He sits among the dead in spirit, waiting to join them in body.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The image of walls and chains is literal for those under siege—the city walls imprison as much as protect. The prisoner cannot go out; his chains are heavy. He knows what it means to be caged.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He cries and calls for help, as anyone would. But his prayer does not ascend—God Himself shuts it out. This is the deepest loneliness: not that he suffers, but that his cry is silenced before it reaches heaven. The words die at the throne.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cut stone is no accident; it is deliberate work. His ways are walled up by intention, his paths made crooked. There is no straight road left. He cannot see forward or find his way. The Lord has locked every exit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bear and lion are ancient Middle Eastern predators—not metaphor but the terror real travelers knew. He compares God's pursuit to these hunters waiting in ambush. The Lord stalks him with the patience and power of a beast of prey.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Turned aside, pulled to pieces, made desolate—one word after another for undoing. His direction is reversed, his body torn, his soul emptied. Complete dissolution. Yet he still stands to testify about it; he is not yet dead.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A bow bent and he is the mark—a living target. In war, marksmen choose their targets. He has been chosen. This is not random; God has aimed at him specifically, and he knows it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The shafts enter his kidneys—the seat of life and strength in ancient thought. God's arrows have pierced to the very source of his being. He is dying by degrees from the inside.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His people mock him—he has become their derision, their song all day. The very community he belonged to has turned him into a jest. Their laughter is as constant as their survival depends on it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Filled with bitterness, sated with wormwood—his inner life has become poison. Not a little taste of it, but full and complete. He has drunk deep of what is bitter, and there is no relief.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Teeth broken with gravel stones, covered with ashes—his mouth is destroyed and his body defiled. These are not metaphors but marks of the deepest shame and degradation in the ancient world. He is unmade.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My soul far off from peace, prosperity forgotten—he has lost not just comfort but the memory of it. Peace is no longer even a dream. He cannot imagine ever knowing it again.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He says aloud what the trial has taught him: his strength is gone, and his hope in the Lord is gone with it. This is despair speaking plainly. The darkness has become so thick that he believes it is total and eternal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Remember my affliction—he asks God not to forget what he has endured. Wormwood and gall are the very taste of his suffering. He wants it witnessed, not by the happy, but by the God who watches all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His soul remembers and is bowed down—the memory of suffering holds him down even as he sits. He cannot escape it by distraction. The weight is internal now, carried in his own bones.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This I recall to my mind—a turning point. Out of the darkness, he chooses to remember something else, something true. Not because the suffering has vanished, but because hope is a choice, an act of will and memory. Therefore I have hope.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh's loving kindnesses keep us from being consumed—the mercies of the Lord are active, defensive. They stand between us and annihilation. His compassion does not fail; it never runs dry. This is the ground of the whole turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: New every morning—generations have read this and found it true. Readers today hear an echo of their own mornings breaking, their own mercies renewed when they thought the night was final. God does not run out of fresh mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh is my portion—not wealth, not health, not the approval of others, but the Lord Himself is what he claims. This is the affirmation of a man with nothing else. Yet in this claim, he has everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Good to those who wait for him—not to those who demand quick answers or easy healing, but to the soul who keeps seeking, who waits. The Lord is good to the persistent seeker, the one who will not let Him go.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Good that a man should hope and wait quietly for the salvation of Yahweh—not to thrash, not to despair, but to wait in faith. Quiet waiting is itself a form of obedience when the trial is long.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth—the discipline early in life teaches what softness never could. A young soul formed under hardship learns trust deeper than pleasure could teach. The yoke is a tool of formation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sit alone and keep silence—in trials, there is a place for words, but also a place for quiet. He lets the Lord lay the burden and sits with it, not fighting, not explaining away. Silence before God is itself a prayer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mouth in the dust, if so be there may be hope—the lowest posture, the dust where death dwells, and yet with *if*. There is a thin thread of possibility even in this humiliation. Perhaps hope awaits on the other side of complete surrender.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Give his cheek to him who strikes—an image found also in the suffering servant passages. Complete non-resistance, accepting reproach without retaliation. The cheek turned is the soul resigned to the Lord's will.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord will not cast off forever—a word that breaks through the darkness like dawn. Forever is a long time; the casting off is not permanent. The trial has an end, and God's grace will not be forever absent.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Though he cause grief, yet he will have compassion—the two truths held together: God causes the grief, and God also will have compassion. They are not contradictory but the shape of His mercy within trial.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men—there is reluctance in God's discipline. He does not delight in suffering as such. His corrections are for good, not for cruelty, though the trial may feel cruel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To crush under foot all the prisoners of the earth—the Lord disapproves of such cruel justice. Those wielding power who abuse the powerless stand against His nature. He is the defender of those crushed by human cruelty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To turn aside the right of a man before the Most High—injustice, the twisting of judgment, stands opposed to God's character. He sees through all the false reasoning that rulers use to justify oppression.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To subvert a man in his cause—perverting justice, destroying the case of the innocent—the Lord does not approve. These evils are written into His nature as violations of His character. He abhors them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Who speaks and it comes to pass when the Lord doesn't command it?—all that happens is under His permission or direction. Nothing escapes His knowledge or sovereignty. This is both comfort and sobering truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Evil and good come out of the mouth of the Most High—He permits both, speaks both into being according to His purposes. This is the hard truth: God is sovereign over all, not just the pleasant parts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Why does a living man complain for the punishment of his sins?—a question that calls the speaker back to reality. He is alive; he is being punished; it is just. To complain as if it were unjust is to miss the point entirely. Acceptance is the path forward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let us search and try our ways—a corporate turning. Not blame, not denial, but honest self-examination. The city must look at itself, its choices, and return to the Lord. This is the beginning of repentance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lift up our heart with our hands to God in the heavens—a physical gesture of prayer, hands and heart raised together. The whole person turning, not just the mind. This is prayer with the body as well as the soul.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We have transgressed and have rebelled. You have not pardoned—the city confesses its guilt plainly. No excuses, no deflection. And yet they cry out that God has not yet pardoned, calling for His mercy even in judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Covered with anger, pursued, killed, not pitied—the full weight of God's wrath is described. Not passive abandonment but active divine pursuit and judgment. And yet the cry for pity continues. Prayer does not cease even under wrath.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Covered yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through—the barrier between God and His people is sealed. The cloud of His anger stands between them. Even prayer cannot pierce it. The silence of God in judgment is terrible.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Made us off-scouring and refuse in the middle of the peoples—not just conquered but despised, treated as garbage. The shame is public, total. They are the discarded of the world, and they know it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All our enemies have opened their mouth wide against us—the surrounding nations circle like predators, gloating. The opened mouth is mockery, hunger, threat. The city is besieged not just militarily but spiritually.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Terror and the pit have come on us, devastation and destruction—a cascade of calamities, each worse than the last. The pit is death itself. All horrors are falling on them at once. Yet they still speak; they still pray.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My eye runs down with streams of water for the destruction of the daughter of my people—the speaker weeps for Jerusalem, for the people of the city. His tears are not for himself alone but for the collective suffering he has witnessed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My eye pours down and doesn't cease—the weeping is endless, without pause. There is so much to grieve that the tears do not stop. The supply of sorrow is infinite.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Until Yahweh looks down and sees from heaven—the weeping continues until God notices. The cry rises from the depths, waiting for the Lord to turn His gaze downward in recognition and response.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My eye affects my soul because of all the daughters of my city—the suffering of the women and children tears at his very being. The sight of the vulnerable undone breaks something in him. He cannot be unmoved.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chased like a bird relentlessly—the ancient hunter's image of pursuit with no mercy, no escape. His enemies track him as if he were prey. And worse: they do it without cause, for no real transgression against them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cut off my life in the dungeon—he is imprisoned, cast into darkness. A stone is cast upon him, sealing the dungeon. They mean to entomb him while alive. Complete helplessness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Waters flowed over my head; I said, I am cut off—drowning in affliction, he declares himself dead. The metaphor becomes near literal: water filling the dungeon, no way out. He has given up hope of rescue.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I called on your name, Yahweh, out of the lowest dungeon—even in the depths, he calls out. Not silence but prayer from the very bottom. The name of the Lord is what he grasps when all else fails.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You heard my voice—God did not keep His ear closed. The prayer from the dungeon was heard. Don't hide your ear from sighing and cry—a plea for continued listening, for God to remain attentive to his distress.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You came near in the day that I called on you—the Lord drew close. And in His nearness, He spoke: 'Don't be afraid.' The word itself is healing. Terror retreats when the Lord says it is time to trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You have pleaded the causes of my soul; you have redeemed my life—the Lord became his advocate, his redeemer. He took up the case and won. The speaker's life has been bought back from death.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh, you have seen my wrong—nothing escapes God's sight. All the injustice done to him is witnessed by the Lord. And because He sees, there is hope that He will judge the cause rightly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You have seen all their vengeance and all their devices against me—the plots and cruelties of his enemies are all known to God. Nothing is hidden from Him; no malice goes unrecorded.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You have heard their reproach, Yahweh—even the mocking, the curses, the insults are heard by God. He is aware of every word spoken against the speaker, every contempt poured out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lips of those that rose up against me and their device against me all day long—constant plotting, constant speech against him. His enemies do not rest; they scheme and speak without ceasing. And the Lord hears it all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You see their sitting down and their rising up—whether at rest or in action, whether planning or executing, their every moment is seen by God. He is aware of their existence itself, not just their deeds. I am their song—he remains an object of mockery, their constant jest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You will render to them a recompense according to the work of their hands—judgment will come. The Lord will repay them according to what they have done. Justice is not lost but deferred to His hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You will give them hardness of heart, your curse to them—not just outward punishment but the internal sealing off from God. Their hearts will harden; they will be given over to their hardness. This is the curse: a soul turned away from the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You will pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of Yahweh—the final word is judgment. As they pursued the speaker, the Lord will pursue them. Destruction is the end of those who rise up against God's people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
